# ivue@2.3.0

<p class="release-head"><a class="release-gh" href="https://github.com/infinite-system/ivue/releases/tag/ivue%402.3.0" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer">View on GitHub ↗</a><span class="release-date">Released August 23, 2026</span></p>

Feature release — one new export, zero breaking changes, and the core
engine untouched: `ivue/extras` gains **`LazyShared`**, the cell that
closes the last open seam in the class-module system. The primary
`ivue` entry stays the bare 1.1 kB engine.

## `LazyShared` — the safe shared-store cell

A shared static store has to hold two properties at once, and until
now JavaScript made you pick one:

- **Load-lazy** — a `static readonly` field initializer runs at module
  load, so constructing another module's class there races the import
  cycle. `$`-cached static getters defer correctly — but they cache
  **per receiver**, so a subclass reads a fresh, empty copy.
- **Unforkable** — one value per process, every access path — base
  class, subclass, `$`-cache — converging on the same object.

`LazyShared` is both. The field eagerly stores the *cell*; the cell
holds an inert thunk; the value constructs on first read — after every
import cycle has resolved — and memoizes **inside the cell**, never on
a receiver, so there is nothing forkable at the end of any access
path:

```ts
import { LazyShared } from 'ivue/extras';

class $SearchRegistry {
  protected static readonly sharedBackend = new LazyShared(
    () => new SearchBackend.Class(),
  );

  protected static get $backend() {
    return this.sharedBackend.value;
  }
}
```

The surface is three members — `new LazyShared(make)`, `.value`,
`.reset()` (the test seam) — and two failure modes are engineered
rather than left to chance: a thunk cycle throws a named error that
tells you which dependency to break, and a throwing thunk never
poisons the cell (the next read retries).

With it, the combined `Reactive()` + `Static()` system is memoizable
at every scope — instance, receiver, shared — with polymorphism,
inheritance, and performance intact. The full map, every value kind in
working code: [Bulletproof class modules](https://ivue.dev/blog/bulletproof-class-modules).

## The Standard, grown again

`npx ivue skill` ships the current Standard Operating Manual
(845 → 1,033 lines), with the conventions that landed alongside the
new cell:

- **`self` — the one cast per class.** Instance code reads its own
  statics through `protected get self() { return this.constructor as
  typeof $X }` — late-bound, so subclass overrides are honored, and
  declared once beside the statics it types instead of asserted at
  every call site. Measured: ~2 ns per read over an inline cast; the
  hoisted `const self = this.self` form in loops measures *faster*
  than inline casts (~0.4 ns vs ~4 ns per iteration, Node 26,
  production build).
- **The shared-store split as two questions.** Does a subclass get its
  own copy (memo → `$`-getter) or not (registry → `static readonly`
  field pin)? And does construction cross a module boundary (→ the
  field holds a `LazyShared` cell)?
- **Restructured for coherence**: the manual now reads as three parts —
  the `Reactive()` instance world, the static world from `ivue/extras`,
  and the style contract.

## Docs

- New guide page: [Caches, Registries & `self`](https://ivue.dev/guide/caches-and-registries)
  — the fork trap, the static-field pin, the load-order boundary,
  `LazyShared`, and the `self` idiom, with the decision table.
- New posts: [Bulletproof class modules](https://ivue.dev/blog/bulletproof-class-modules)
  and [The Options API everyone actually wanted](https://ivue.dev/blog/the-options-api-everyone-wanted).

## Numbers

- Core `ivue` entry: byte-identical to 2.2.2 — 1.1 kB gzipped, zero
  dependencies.
- `ivue/extras` grows by the ~40-line cell; engine and extras test
  coverage stays 100%.
